title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Guideline From the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association
shortTitle: AHA/ASA 2026: update ED thrombolysis, thrombectomy and BP pathways
summary: The replacement acute ischemic stroke guideline supports either alteplase or tenecteplase within 4.5 hours, selected extended-window treatment, and broader thrombectomy eligibility. It distinguishes disabling from nondisabling deficits and advises against intensive systolic BP reduction below 140 mm Hg after reperfusion.
whyItMatters: Update stroke alerts and transfer pathways with the stroke service. A low NIHSS alone should not dismiss a disabling deficit, while nondisabling presentations require a different antithrombotic pathway.
limitations: Eligibility is population- and imaging-specific. Pediatric interventional recommendations have less mature evidence; this summary cannot replace the complete treatment algorithms.
population: Adults with acute ischemic stroke; selected pediatric recommendations.
intervention: Updated prehospital, reperfusion and early inpatient stroke recommendations.
primaryEndpoint: Evidence-based recommendations rather than a single trial endpoint.
findings: Either alteplase or tenecteplase is endorsed within 4.5 hours in eligible patients.
Selected basilar occlusions within 24 hours and NIHSS at least 10 receive a strong EVT recommendation.
Intensive systolic BP lowering below 140 mm Hg after reperfusion is not recommended.
evidenceNotes: AHA Top Things to Know reviewed in full; publisher metadata verifies January 26 first-online date and provides legal PDF. Complete guideline text was not reviewed. Publisher indicates a correction; precise dosing should be checked against current guideline.
